D-01_ff.reason: An exact-SMILES, peer-reviewed neat-bulk-PEEK MD study (Chen et al. 2023, 10.1021/acsami.3c01307) used PCFF+ with pppm electrostatics and reports density -3.9% vs experiment (1.22 vs 1.27 g/cm3) -- same sign and comparable magnitude to PolyJarvis's own measured PCFF density deficit (-5.1%). This resolves the sign ambiguity the plan's own D-01 evidence flagged against the PEEK2020 cyclic-oligomer/COMPASS-II result (+2.2%, opposite sign): that discrepancy is attributable to the cyclic-oligomer structural model, not to Class-II force fields underpredicting PEEK density in general. Combined with the same paper's pppm electrostatics and the PEEK2020 Class-II Tg validation (COMPASS II 424-429 K vs exp 418 K, +1.5-2.5%), the literature record now directly and consistently supports pcff for this exact SMILES.

dominant_uncertainty: Both peer-reviewed density validations are on structural models that differ from this run's linear amorphous 10-chain/DP18 melt (one is a nanocomposite paper's neat-matrix baseline, the other a small cyclic oligomer), so the ~-4 to -5% PCFF density deficit is well-corroborated in sign but not tightly bounded in magnitude for this exact cell.
notes: The evidence-store exact-SMILES hit for this SMILES (record 602a28517726, provenance source_run=PEEK_1) shows this polymer was literature-critiqued before under this same run name; this pass reused and extended that grounding rather than re-searching from scratch, per the skip-fresh-search rule for exact_smiles peer_reviewed_doi hits.

sources.claim: This MD/DFT study on a catechol-based cyclic-oligomer PEEK model cites its own experimental Tg comparison target as 418.2 K, and reports its own COMPASS II MD-simulated Tg (424.4-428.6 K) as 'close to' this experimental value (+1.5 to +2.5%). This independently corroborates polymer_rules.json's existing experimental_tg_K.PEEK=418 entry.

Neat bulk-PEEK MD (PCFF+, pppm, 500 K/1 atm NPT production after an 800 atm/750 K anneal) gives density 1.22 g/cm3 vs experimental 1.27 g/cm3 for amorphous PEEK (-3.9%) -- same sign and comparable magnitude to PolyJarvis's own measured PCFF density deficit (-5.1%), a direct same-chemistry confirmation.

COMPASS II (Class II family, same lineage as PCFF) MD Tg for a PEEK cyclic-oligomer model: unit-cell 424.4 K, supercell 428.6 K vs exp 418 K (+1-3% error); density 1.364 vs exp 1.328 g/cm3 (+2.2%, opposite sign from the linear-chain PCFF result above, attributable to the cyclic-oligomer structural model rather than the force-field family).

MD study on five novel poly(phthalazinone ether sulfone ketone) (PPESK) polymers -- an aromatic ether-sulfone-ketone backbone chemically adjacent to PKTN/PSFO -- used COMPASS, described by the authors as 'a typical PCFF type force field ... proved suitable for polymer and energetic materials', for CED/solubility-parameter and mechanical-property predictions; no experimental Tg/density comparison was recoverable, so this only corroborates PCFF-family suitability for this backbone chemistry class, not a signed error.

Long-range Coulombic interactions for a PEEK(-CNT) system were computed with a particle-particle particle-mesh (pppm) solver (LJ cutoff 20 A), using PCFF+ intramolecular parameters and MedeA forcefield-assign partial charges.
